questions.prompt: In this course's framework, what is an architecture constraint, as distinct from a requirement or an assumption?
options: A fixed boundary the design cannot change, usually imposed from outside the project
Something the solution must do or provide for the business
A stated, unconfirmed belief the design is built on, flagged so it can be revisited
Any requirement that happens to be difficult or expensive to implement
questions.explain: A constraint is a fixed boundary you cannot design around because it's imposed from outside the project — distinct from a requirement (what the solution must do) and an assumption (an unconfirmed belief flagged for later review).
questions.distractorExplain: Option B describes a requirement, not a constraint — a requirement specifies what the solution must do, while a constraint is a boundary that already exists and cannot be changed by the design at all.

questions.prompt: LTV Global's VP of Sales insists during intake that 'the new system must talk to our ERP in real time — no exceptions.' Based on this course's current-state landscape analysis, which system actually cannot support real-time integration under any design?
options: Meridian ERP
LedgerPoint
Snowflake
Okta
questions.explain: LedgerPoint is the mainframe-based financial system with no API at all, reachable only through batch SFTP file transfer — Meridian ERP, by contrast, exposes SOAP and REST endpoints and can support near-real-time integration.

questions.prompt: Select every item this course identifies as one of LTV Global's real business drivers for this transformation.
options: Fragmentation across business units seeing incomplete, disconnected pictures of the same customers
Growth straining processes built for a smaller, North America-centric company
A government mandate requiring every multinational to adopt Salesforce
The rising cost of maintaining EuroCRM and reconciling data by hand
Competitive pressure from dealers expecting modern self-service
questions.explain: The four real business drivers are fragmentation, growth, cost, and competitive pressure — there is no government mandate in this scenario; that option was never stated as a driver.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: LTV Global operates in three regions — North America, EMEA, and ________.
questions.explain: APAC (Australia, Singapore, Japan) is LTV Global's third region — the newest and fastest-growing, with the least legacy debt of the three.

questions.prompt: Match each LTV Global stakeholder to their primary concern about this transformation.
right: Performance and scale of the highest-transaction-volume business unit
Caution about touching the legacy financial system
Zero disruption to technicians during the EuroCRM cutover
GDPR compliance and the company's overall risk posture
questions.explain: Each stakeholder's concern traces to their role: the Parts & Aftermarket VP to performance at the highest-volume unit, the CFO to the financial system's risk, the Field Service Director to migration disruption, and the Security/Compliance Officer to GDPR and overall risk.

questions.prompt: In general data-architecture terms, what does 'system of record' mean?
options: Any system that happens to hold a backup copy of a given dataset
The system with the fastest query performance for a given object
The one system whose data is treated as authoritative for a given category of information
The system responsible for enforcing multi-factor authentication
questions.explain: A system of record is the one system treated as authoritative for a category of data when systems disagree — the foundation of LTV Global's data-ownership map.
questions.distractorExplain: Holding a backup copy (the first option) does not make a system authoritative — a system of record is specifically the source of truth, not merely a system that happens to contain a copy of the data.

questions.prompt: Why did LTV Global choose a single global Salesforce org instead of a separate org per region or business unit?
options: A multi-org estate is technically impossible for any company with more than three business units
The target-state vision commits to a unified customer view across business units, which no multi-org estate can deliver natively
Single-org is always the universally correct choice regardless of company structure
Salesforce no longer permits multi-org licensing for enterprise customers
questions.explain: The single-org decision follows directly from the vision's unified-customer-view commitment — no native Salesforce report can span two separate orgs, which would undercut that specific requirement.

questions.prompt: Why does LTV Global's data model use a lookup (not master-detail) relationship from Parts Order to Equipment Asset?
options: Lookup relationships are required for any object with a custom name
Parts Order is the highest-volume object in the design, and master-detail would force it to inherit Equipment Asset's sharing-recalculation cost at a volume where that becomes a real performance risk
Master-detail relationships cannot be created on custom objects
Equipment Asset does not support any relationships to other custom objects
questions.explain: The relationship type is a deliberate consequence of Parts Order's extreme volume — a lookup avoids forcing costly sharing-recalculation inheritance that master-detail would impose at that scale.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about LTV Global's resolution of ownership/data skew risk on the Parts Order object.
options: Parts Order records are owned by region/business-unit queues rather than a single integration user
Queue ownership also gives regional parts teams a natural, pre-filtered work queue as a side benefit
A single Meridian integration user owning every record is the current, accepted design
Queue-based ownership distributes records across a structure Salesforce's sharing engine already handles well
Ownership skew only matters for objects using Person Accounts
questions.explain: Queue-based ownership (not a single integration user) resolves the ownership-skew risk, distributing records across a sharing-friendly structure while also giving regional teams a useful work queue — ownership skew is a general LDV concern, not limited to Person Account-related objects.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Equipment Asset's serial number field is marked as an indexed ________ specifically so lookups by serial number stay selective and fast as the object grows past millions of rows.
questions.explain: Serial_Number__c is marked as an indexed external ID, keeping the most common query pattern on Equipment Asset selective at large data volumes.

questions.prompt: Why does LTV Global route all integration traffic through a central hub instead of direct point-to-point connections between systems?
options: Point-to-point integration doesn't scale past the first few connections and creates no reusable logic, while a hub concentrates integration logic where it can be documented and maintained
Point-to-point integration is forbidden by Salesforce's terms of service
A central hub is always faster at runtime than any direct connection
Named Credentials only function when a hub is present
questions.explain: The hub decision is about maintainability and scale: each new point-to-point connection multiplies integration surface area with no reuse, while a hub concentrates and documents the logic.

questions.prompt: Why does Meridian ERP integration use a synchronous REST callout for order creation but a nightly Bulk API batch for product/inventory sync?
options: Order creation needs an immediate confirmed/rejected response, while inventory data doesn't need second-by-second accuracy, so batch is cheaper and more predictable
Meridian cannot support any synchronous integration at all
Bulk API cannot be used for order creation under any circumstances
Product and inventory data changes too frequently to ever be batched
questions.explain: The two Meridian integration paths are matched to two different freshness needs — a rep or dealer needs immediate order confirmation, while inventory levels can tolerate a predictable nightly batch cadence.

questions.prompt: Why does this course insist LedgerPoint's nightly batch integration is 'the correct design, not a compromise'?
options: Because batch integration is always technically superior to real-time integration
Because LedgerPoint has no API and modernizing it is outside this transformation's scope, so a carefully engineered batch-with-reconciliation design is the right answer given that fixed constraint
Because the CFO personally prefers batch-based systems
Because Meridian's synchronous integration proves real-time integration is never actually necessary
questions.explain: Given LedgerPoint's fixed no-API constraint, a deliberately engineered batch-with-reconciliation design is the correct answer, not a lesser substitute for a 'real' integration that was never achievable within this project's scope.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about LTV Global's three external API integrations.
options: The parts-pricing/catalog API uses External Services so the Dealer Portal's declarative tools can call it directly
The credit/financing-check API's results inherit the same field-level security restrictions as the credit-score fields they populate
All three external APIs use the exact same integration mechanism for consistency
The shipping-carrier tracking API is pulled on demand via a plain Apex callout
Named Credentials are used to centralize authentication details for all three APIs
questions.explain: Each external API uses the mechanism that fits its usage pattern (External Services for the pricing API's declarative need, Apex callouts for the on-demand shipping and credit-check lookups) rather than one uniform mechanism, and all three use Named Credentials with the credit-check results protected by the same field-level security as the fields they populate.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Salesforce feeds LTV Global's Snowflake data warehouse through a nightly ________ extraction, the API designed for large, asynchronous data volumes.
questions.explain: Bulk API is used for the nightly Snowflake extraction because it's designed for exactly this kind of large, asynchronous data-volume job, as opposed to a synchronous API meant for smaller, real-time operations.

questions.prompt: Why does LTV Global maintain a dedicated integration sandbox, separate from any single business unit's own sandbox?
options: Because the integration hub is shared across all four business units, and a dedicated sandbox catches cross-BU integration conflicts before they reach staging
Because Salesforce prohibits more than one sandbox type per org
Because business-unit sandboxes cannot technically connect to any external system
Because the integration sandbox replaces the need for a staging environment entirely
questions.explain: Since all four business units depend on the same shared integration hub, a dedicated, separately-owned integration sandbox is where cross-BU changes to that hub get tested against each other before reaching staging.

questions.prompt: Why does LTV Global's Change Advisory Board (CAB) review only changes touching shared metadata or the integration hub, rather than every single release?
options: Because full review of every change would make the CAB a bottleneck, while BU-specific changes with no shared dependency carry no cross-BU risk
Because the CAB has no actual authority to block any release
Because only Equipment Financing's changes ever touch shared metadata
Because CAB review is only required once per fiscal year
questions.explain: Full CAB review on every change would make it a bottleneck; limiting mandatory review to changes with genuine cross-BU/shared-metadata risk keeps the process proportionate to the actual risk involved.

questions.prompt: Put LTV Global's CI pipeline stages in the correct order, from a developer's committed change to a production-eligible release.
items: Developer commits metadata changes to version control from a scratch org
CI pipeline automatically runs Apex tests against the change in a clean environment
Peer review happens against the committed change
Change deploys to the integration sandbox (if it touches integration logic) or staging
Staging validation, including load testing, completes before production eligibility
questions.explain: The pipeline moves from commit, through automated testing (a gate no change bypasses), peer review, environment deployment, and finally staging validation before a change becomes eligible for production.

questions.prompt: Put LTV Global's three migration waves in the order they actually run, per the migration strategy.
items: Wave 1: EMEA, with EuroCRM retirement and a parallel-run period
Wave 2: North America, consolidating legacy point solutions and process variation
Wave 3: APAC, a lighter-footprint rollout benefiting from the earlier waves
questions.explain: EMEA goes first because it's the hardest, most disruption-sensitive migration (EuroCRM retirement); North America follows to consolidate its own fragmented processes; APAC goes last because it has the least legacy debt and benefits from lessons learned earlier.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: during EuroCRM's retirement, LTV Global uses a ________ period, where EuroCRM and the equivalent Salesforce functionality both operate and stay in sync, before EuroCRM is formally decommissioned.
questions.explain: The parallel-run period gives EMEA Field Service technicians a fallback if the new Salesforce-based process reveals a gap, directly resolving the risk of EuroCRM's cutover disrupting the team.

questions.prompt: Why should the data model diagram use master-detail notation specifically for the Service Contract to Equipment Asset relationship, rather than a plain line?
options: Plain lines are not supported by any diagramming convention
The relationship type itself is architecturally meaningful, and the diagram's notation should let a reviewer see it without needing the supporting prose to explain it
Service Contract has no actual relationship to Equipment Asset in this design
Master-detail relationships cannot be represented visually in any diagram
questions.explain: The diagram's notation should carry the information that this is master-detail (not lookup), since that relationship type was chosen deliberately and a reviewer shouldn't need the prose to discover it.

questions.prompt: Why does this course keep the integration landscape diagram and the security/sharing diagram as two separate artifacts?
options: Because combining them is technically impossible in any diagramming tool
Because they convey fundamentally different kinds of information (data flow vs. visibility), and combining them would make neither story read clearly
Because integration and security have no real relationship to each other in this design
Because Salesforce requires every architecture engagement to produce exactly two diagrams
questions.explain: The decision is a usability one: a reader asking an integration question wants an uncluttered integration diagram, and a reader asking a security question wants the reverse — the TAD's prose is where the two domains' connections get explained.

questions.prompt: What is the critical component that separates a real architecture decision record (ADR) from a plain design summary?
options: Including a cost estimate for the chosen option
Naming the rejected alternatives and the specific reason each was rejected, not just describing what was chosen
Formatting the record as a slide rather than a document
Listing every stakeholder who attended the meeting where the decision was made
questions.explain: A design summary only describes what was chosen; a real ADR also names what wasn't chosen and the specific reason, which is what lets a future reader or review board judge whether alternatives were genuinely considered.

questions.prompt: Select every item that is one of this course's five key architecture decision records (ADRs) for LTV Global.
options: Single global org vs. multi-org
Central integration hub vs. point-to-point integration
LedgerPoint batch integration vs. forcing real-time
Choosing Salesforce over a competing CRM platform
Summarized vs. full general-ledger replication into Salesforce
questions.explain: The five named ADRs cover org strategy, the integration hub, LedgerPoint's batch design, GL replication scope, and external identity federation — this course never frames choosing Salesforce itself as one of the decision records, since that choice was already fixed by the scenario.

questions.prompt: Match each deliverable to what it is specifically responsible for communicating.
right: Objects and relationships, without field-level detail
Field-level detail for each object, such as types and purposes
Impact, likelihood, and mitigation for each identified risk
questions.explain: Each deliverable has a distinct, non-overlapping job: the ERD shows structure, the dictionary shows field detail, the risk register tracks risk and mitigation, and the roadmap sequences the build by dependency.

questions.prompt: Why is 'I don't know, but here's how I'd find out' considered a legitimate, strong answer during an Architecture Review Board defense?
options: It avoids the question entirely with no consequence to the architect's credibility
It demonstrates knowing where the real answer lives, which is stronger than inventing a confident-sounding but unfounded guess
Board members never ask about details outside a prepared script
It is only acceptable if the question concerns a risk rated as low likelihood
questions.explain: Naming the correct mechanism to resolve a genuine gap is a stronger, more credible response than fabricating a specific-sounding answer that isn't actually grounded in anything.

questions.prompt: In the mock defense, a board member calls LTV Global's three different integration mechanisms (synchronous, batch, event-driven) 'inconsistent.' What is the strongest defense of this apparent inconsistency?
options: Conceding the design is inconsistent and should be unified into one mechanism
Explaining that the three systems aren't actually equivalent — each mechanism is the correct answer to that specific system's real constraint, not an arbitrary choice
Refusing to engage with the question as unfair
Claiming all three systems secretly use the same mechanism already
questions.explain: The strong defense reframes apparent inconsistency as three independently correct answers to three genuinely different constraints — Meridian's real-time capability, LedgerPoint's lack of any API, and Snowflake's batch-friendly analytics needs.

questions.prompt: What does LTV Global's Architecture Review Board ultimately decide at the end of the final defense?
options: Unconditional rejection, requiring a complete redesign
Approved with conditions — specific, narrow follow-up items (a LedgerPoint load test and an Equipment Financing security audit) tied to work already named earlier in the course
Unconditional approval with no further action required
A decision deferred indefinitely with no outcome given at all
questions.explain: The board approves the design with two specific, narrow conditions — a realistic and common outcome, not a sign of underlying design failure.

questions.prompt: Match each of LTV Global's three defense phases to what happens during it.
right: The architect walks the board through the design using the executive presentation as the visual spine
Board members ask about any of the thirteen design areas in any order
The board renders its decision, such as approval with conditions
questions.explain: The three phases are sequential and distinct: present the design, defend it under open questioning, and receive the board's final decision.

questions.prompt: Put these post-defense steps in the correct order, from the board's decision to the design being fully, unconditionally approved.
items: Board issues an 'approved with conditions' outcome
The LedgerPoint reconciliation process is load-tested against realistic batch volume
The Equipment Financing field-level security configuration is independently audited
Both conditions are satisfied and documented
The design moves from 'approved with conditions' to simply 'approved'
questions.explain: Closing out an 'approved with conditions' outcome requires actually completing and documenting each named condition before the design can be considered unconditionally approved — the conditions are real work, not a formality.
